reading: Every solid square loses its outer ring (9x9->7x7, 5x5->3x3, 3x3->1x1) and every single cell grows into a 9x9 square centred on it, so square sizes cycle 1->9->7->5->3->1.

slots.subject: each solid single-colour square object
slots.size_map: side s becomes s-2, side 1 becomes 9

why: each output object has the same colour and centre as an input object and side length cycled down by 2 (1 wraps to 9)

reading: Each object loses its two leftmost columns: those cells become background (objects 2 columns wide vanish).

new_rows.name: left2
new_rows.datalog:
minx(O, min(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X), cell(Y, X, C).
left2(Y, X) :- obj(O, Y, X), cell(Y, X, C), minx(O, M), M2 = M + 2, X < M2.

why: every changed cell lies in the leftmost two columns of its object and becomes the background colour 8; nothing else changes
invariants: cells of each object from its third column on

reading: Two overlapping shapes swap their stacking order: in the overlap, the shape that was underneath is drawn on top, so the hidden shape becomes complete.

slots.subject: pairs of overlapping single-colour shapes (rectangles / straight bars)
slots.overlap: cells where the top shape covers the hidden shape's completed box/line
slots.result: overlap cells take the hidden shape's colour

why: only overlap cells change, and each becomes the colour of the shape whose bounding box/line is incomplete in the input

reading: Each colour-4 rectangle holding N dots of colour c gets a surrounding ring of colour c, N cells thick.

slots.subject: each colour-4 rectangle containing dots
slots.colour: the colour of its inner dots

why: around every rectangle the ring width equals its dot count and the ring colour equals the dot colour

reading: Plus shapes whose centres lie on a common diagonal are joined by a diagonal line of colour 2 through the background between them.

slots.subject: plus-shaped objects of colour 3
slots.pairs: two pluses whose centres share a diagonal (|dy|=|dx|)
slots.line: colour 2 on the background cells of that diagonal between them

why: every new colour-2 cell lies on a diagonal joining the centres of two pluses

reading: Every object moves straight up by a distance equal to its own height.

slots.subject: each object
slots.distance: the object's own height (bounding box rows)

why: each output object has the input object's shape and colour, shifted up by its height; old cells are cleared

reading: The whole 3x3 grid is filled with its most frequent colour.

slots.colour: the most common colour of the input

why: every output cell equals the input's most frequent colour

reading: A colour-9 skeleton stays fixed; every other coloured piece attached to it slides straight away from the 9 it touches until it reaches the grid border, keeping its shape.

new_rows.name: not9
new_rows.datalog:
nine(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, 9).
not9(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !nine(Y, X).

why: each non-9 piece keeps its shape and ends touching the border in the direction pointing away from the adjacent 9; 9 cells never move
invariants: shape and colour of each piece

reading: The colour-3 shape is pushed against the full colour-2 wall line, and a full line of colour 8 is drawn parallel to the wall right behind the shape on the far side.
verb: push to wall and back with line

slots.subject: the colour-3 shape (largest object)
slots.move: slide subject perpendicular to the wall until it touches it
slots.line: full row/column of colour 8 adjacent to the subject on the side away from the wall

why: the 3 shape keeps its shape and touches the 2 wall; one full 8 line sits immediately behind it

reading: A 2x2 colour key sits in a corner; the dots of the dotted square field are recoloured by quadrant: dots in each quadrant of the field take the key colour in the same position of the key.

slots.key: the 2x2 multi-colour block in a corner, beyond the 8 border strip
slots.field: the square background area holding single-colour dots
slots.rule: split the field into 4 equal quadrants; dots in quadrant (i,j) become key[i][j]

why: each dot's new colour equals the key cell in the same quadrant position; non-dot cells are unchanged
